The old man, this Hare Parka old man, said to the daughters -in-law: âBring lard, bring food. Bring everything there is. The Nenets will come tomorrow, theyâll eat.â The old man said so. They brought food. Inside this house they covered the floor with new hay. The old man started giving food to the Nenets. Ouch! The next day the Nenets gathered together. An army of thirty people.[OSV:] "jap tattÉ¨qo" - "to meet together". [They look], in the empty tent the Hare Parka old man is [sitting] together with the daughters-in-law. They lay down fresh hay. He also had a wife [an old woman]. [The old man] told the daughters-in-law to go. âGo out into the street. Take the children into the street.â The old man is hanging on, giving the people to eat. One morning men arrived. They eat. He is putting big logs into the stove. [the fire] is burning. He sent the daughters-in-law outside for no reason. They lit a fire outdoors. They lit a fire, and from the fire they lit birchbark torches. This way they used to dry something. âYouâll be here, Iâll go out.â [The Nenets] are eating. The Nenets are saying: âGrandfather, why are you putting so much wood into the stove? Wonât the fire burn the stove?â âIt wonât.â That is how the Hare Parka old man in rags made them be there. He is running [around] by the stove next to the big door. Once a burning log fell into the house from the outside. [The Hare Parka old man] rushed [away]. The Nenets men almost caught the old man by the door, all they grabbed was a piece of the hare parka. It looks like he went out through the window of the house. There were two windows. He had a big house! He covered it with fire, put up wooden poles, [sticking them into the ground] a big axe handle deep. Those [daughters-in-law] were throwing fire into the house. Earlier they had thrown gunpowder under the hay. The fire [gunpowder] blew up suddenly! The army of those thirty men burned to death in the fire. The daughters-in-law set out from upstream. The old man, having run outside, held an axe in his hands. Everyone who had hardly made an appearance outdoors, they hit [those] in the face. The daughters-in-law were throwing fire. They were throwing it down the chimney and through the two windows into the house.[OSV:] 1) The verbal form "qÉË-ÅÉË-tÉ¨t" (throw-PRS-3PL) would be more correct here; 2) the nominal form They burned the house down.
